rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to retain weakly retained compounds while eluting strongly retained compounds, with ample final hold before acquisition ends. The retention and resolution pattern will guide subsequent optimization of gradient range, duration, and temperature.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the last peak's retention time while testing whether the current resolution margin tolerates faster elution. Keep starting composition and temperature fixed to isolate the gradient-slope effect.

The fast gradient eliminated the time penalty but compressed two central pairs. Raising temperature tests whether altered selectivity can resolve that cluster while preserving the short analysis time.

Test an intermediate high temperature to separate the pair nearly co-eluting at 60 C while retaining the improved selectivity within the central cluster. The unchanged fast gradient should keep the time penalty at zero.

Test a shorter gradient at 50 C to balance the temperature-sensitive central separations. Lowering temperature should open the pair compressed at 55–60 C, while the steeper gradient may improve the other central pair without introducing a time penalty.

Probe the low-temperature selectivity regime, where the central pair that crossed between 40 and 55 C may separate in the opposite order. Keeping the 10-minute gradient allows a direct temperature comparison and may retain a negligible time penalty.

Slightly lengthen the best-performing gradient to improve the remaining under-resolved pair at 55 C. The last peak should still elute near the zero-time-penalty window; this run will also test whether the other central pair retains adequate resolution.

The maximum CRF has already been reached; test a slightly shallower neighboring gradient to assess whether another method also attains it. This should improve the 1.59-resolution pair, while checking that the other critical pair and last-peak time remain acceptable.

Test a modestly higher starting organic fraction to shorten retention and probe selectivity around the two critical pairs. The maximum score is already secured; this explores whether an equally scoring method offers a larger resolution margin.

Combine the higher starting fraction with a slightly shallower gradient to improve the remaining under-resolved pair. Based on the neighboring runs, this may preserve zero time penalty while giving both critical pairs resolution above 1.5.

Lower the endpoint another grid step to increase resolution of the remaining critical pair while likely keeping the last peak near 8 minutes. This tests for another maximum-score method with a larger minimum-resolution margin than injection 7.

Test a higher starting fraction with a shallower gradient to balance faster elution against critical-pair resolution. With the maximum CRF already achieved, this explores another potentially optimal method with additional separation margin.

Preserve injection 7’s starting composition, temperature, and gradient slope, but end the ramp earlier at lower organic content. All peaks should elute before the changed portion reaches the outlet, making this a candidate for the same maximum CRF with a lower final organic fraction.

Test a gradient slope between injections 10 and 11 to balance the two critical resolutions while keeping the last peak below 8 minutes. This may match the maximum CRF with more resolution margin than injection 7 and less time penalty risk than injection 11.

With the maximum CRF already achieved, test the temperature sensitivity of injection 14 by lowering temperature one grid step. This isolates selectivity changes and assesses whether its critical-pair resolution survives at 50 C.

Test the upper-temperature neighbor of injection 14 to complete the local selectivity check. The maximum score is already secured, but this run will show whether higher temperature improves the central cluster or creates a new co-elution.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction and steeper gradient move the nearly co-eluting pair at 60 C past its selectivity crossover into useful separation. This explores a faster alternative while retaining the already established maximum-score methods.

Raise the starting organic fraction to push the remaining critical pair farther beyond its selectivity crossover, while lengthening the gradient to protect neighboring separations. This tests whether the faster 60 C regime can also attain the maximum CRF.

Keep the successful gradient slope from injection 7 but switch to a 50% organic hold after 6 minutes. The first nine peaks should be unchanged; this tests whether the last compound still elutes within the zero-time-penalty window at a lower endpoint.

Slightly flatten injection 11’s gradient to increase the separation of its 1.67-resolution pair while checking that the other critical pair stays above 1.5. The last peak is expected near 8.4 minutes, potentially retaining the maximum CRF with more balanced resolution margins.

Preserve injection 11’s gradient slope and temperature while lowering the endpoint to 60% organic. Its last peak eluted before this shorter ramp reaches its endpoint at the outlet, so this method should retain the maximum CRF and 1.58 minimum resolution.

Test a slope between injections 11 and 20, where both critical pairs remained adequately resolved and the time penalty was zero. This should provide another maximum-score method, with a higher endpoint available for washing the column after elution.

Test a lower-endpoint method with a slope between the maximum-scoring injections 20 and 22. It should preserve full resolution and zero time penalty, while reaching its final composition earlier than either method.

Preserve injection 7’s successful starting composition, temperature, and gradient slope with an intermediate endpoint. Because all compounds should elute before the ramp ends, this distinct method is expected to match the maximum CRF of 1.000.

Use the final injection to test a slightly shallower neighbor of injection 24, seeking improved separation of one critical pair while checking that the other remains above 1.5. The campaign has already achieved the maximum possible CRF of 1.000; this tests the boundary of that optimal region.
